description.value:
Transcendent · Withdrawn, Not Dead

Watched what humanity did to itself and to Uriel, and simply left. Heaven's gates locked; Hell stopped taking calls too. Not divine death — a deliberate absence, which means the door is not necessarily closed forever. Vigil is the class built entirely around this: patient, rare, slow to act on any individual scale, aimed at maybe someday earning that attention back.

Full writeup Vigil dossier

pov.text: The public story is grief, and it isn't a lie — watching what happened to Uriel, and to itself, was real. It's just not the whole ledger. Uriel was the stake that made holding a world this far from the center worth the cost. Once the corporations and kingdoms bled that stake dry, the accounting simply changed: a costly, half-abandoned holding, hungered after by something that never stops counting converts, that could no longer be defended from here. Leaving looked like sorrow because sorrow was also true. It was still, underneath that, a withdrawal.
